scenes.tts: The first film stopped new G protein activation with a mark and its reader. What ends the active signal already downstream?
scenes.caption: The first film stopped new G-protein activation with a mark and its reader. What ends the active signal already downstream?
scenes.visual: Reuse the first film's final world and exact color map. Red arrestin blocks the yellow receptor, but a green active G-alpha block, blue messenger pool, and gold-marked target continue moving below it. A question mark travels down the chain. Label cartoons 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: The first film stopped new G-protein activation with a mark and its reader. What ends the active signal already downstream?

scenes.visual: Keep the moving downstream chain dimly visible. Title writes across it: Where the Signal Runs Out.

scenes.tts: Each layer is an active pool with an input and an exit. Receptors produce active G proteins. Active G proteins help produce second messenger. Messenger activates a kinase, which adds phosphate marks to targets.
scenes.caption: Each layer is an active pool with an input and an exit. Receptors produce active G proteins. Active G proteins help produce second messenger. Messenger activates a kinase, which adds phosphate marks to targets.
scenes.visual: Make the chain fill most of the frame. Animate green ON blocks entering the G-protein pool, blue dots entering a messenger tank, and gold badges attaching to target blocks. Put a small IN arrow and OUT arrow beside each pool.
scenes.narration: Each layer is an active pool with an input and an exit. Receptors produce active G proteins. Active G proteins help produce second messenger. Messenger activates a kinase, which adds phosphate marks to targets.

scenes.tts: These pools overlap in time. Stopping new receptor output does not instantly erase G T P, messenger, or target phosphate already present. Each pool keeps changing until its own input and exit settle the balance.
scenes.caption: These pools overlap in time. Stopping new receptor output does not instantly erase GTP, messenger, or target phosphate already present. Each pool keeps changing until its own input and exit settle the balance.
scenes.visual: Close the receptor's input gate at the top. The green, blue, and gold pools continue moving below, then fade at visibly different schematic rates. Keep separate IN and OUT arrows active for each layer.
scenes.narration: These pools overlap in time. Stopping new receptor output does not instantly erase GTP, messenger, or target phosphate already present. Each pool keeps changing until its own input and exit settle the balance.

scenes.tts: G alpha carries G T P while active and hydrolyzes it to G D P. An R G S protein speeds that reaction for compatible G proteins. Faster hydrolysis shortens the lifetime of the active green pool.
scenes.caption: G-alpha carries GTP while active and hydrolyzes it to GDP. An RGS protein speeds that reaction for compatible G proteins. Faster hydrolysis shortens the lifetime of the active green pool.
scenes.visual: Zoom to one green G-alpha block carrying a bright GTP badge. A teal RGS clamp briefly closes around it; the badge transforms to GDP, and the block moves into an inactive tray. Repeat faster with RGS than without it. Mark timing 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: G-alpha carries GTP while active and hydrolyzes it to GDP. An RGS protein speeds that reaction for compatible G proteins. Faster hydrolysis shortens the lifetime of the active green pool.

scenes.tts: A phosphodiesterase drains a cyclic nucleotide pool by opening the messenger's phosphate ring. When synthesis and breakdown match, the pool holds steady. Slower breakdown makes the same input build a higher, longer lasting pool.
scenes.caption: A phosphodiesterase drains a cyclic-nucleotide pool by opening the messenger's phosphate ring. When synthesis and breakdown match, the pool holds steady. Slower breakdown makes the same input build a higher, longer-lasting pool.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the blue messenger tank. Rounded blocks labelled cyclic messenger enter through a pipe labelled synthesis. A teal PDE drain relabels each block '5′-AMP or 5′-GMP' and dims it before exit. Keep both arrows moving. Draw no molecular structure.
scenes.narration: A phosphodiesterase drains a cyclic-nucleotide pool by opening the messenger's phosphate ring. When synthesis and breakdown match, the pool holds steady. Slower breakdown makes the same input build a higher, longer-lasting pool.

scenes.tts: Now shut messenger synthesis off, then inhibit the drain. Can protecting the remaining messenger create a new signal?
scenes.caption: Now shut messenger synthesis off, then inhibit the drain. Can protecting the remaining messenger create a new signal?
scenes.visual: Close the synthesis valve completely. Place a teal inhibitor bar across the PDE drain. The nearly empty blue tank remains centered under the question. A small label says 'production equals zero'.
scenes.narration: Now shut messenger synthesis off, then inhibit the drain. Can protecting the remaining messenger create a new signal?

scenes.visual: Hold the question and empty tank. Let one final blue messenger block drift slowly while both valves remain closed.

scenes.tts: No. No new messenger is made. An empty pool stays empty. Messenger already present is protected and decays more slowly. With continuing input, inhibition raises and prolongs the pool.
scenes.caption: No. No new messenger is made. An empty pool stays empty. Messenger already present is protected and decays more slowly. With continuing input, inhibition raises and prolongs the pool.
scenes.visual: Show three large cases in the same tank, one at a time. Without input, a nearly empty tank stays near zero. Without input, a partly full tank drains more slowly once the drain narrows. With input, the blue level rises when the drain narrows. Transform between cases and clear the previous answer before each label. Mark levels 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: No. No new messenger is made. An empty pool stays empty. Messenger already present is protected and decays more slowly. With continuing input, inhibition raises and prolongs the pool.

scenes.tts: The last pool here is phosphorylated target protein. A kinase adds each gold phosphate badge. A protein phosphatase removes it. The phosphorylated pool fades when removal overtakes new phosphorylation. If that phosphate activates the target, its activity fades too.
scenes.caption: The last pool here is phosphorylated target protein. A kinase adds each gold phosphate badge. A protein phosphatase removes it. The phosphorylated pool fades when removal overtakes new phosphorylation. If that phosphate activates the target, its activity fades too.
scenes.visual: Carry one target block forward. A blue-activated kinase adds gold badges from the left. A teal phosphatase lifts badges from the right. A balance meter tips toward removal, and the target's glow fades.
scenes.narration: The last pool here is phosphorylated target protein. A kinase adds each gold phosphate badge. A protein phosphatase removes it. The phosphorylated pool fades when removal overtakes new phosphorylation. If that phosphate activates the target, its activity fades too.

scenes.tts: Changing an exit changes both amplitude and timing. A narrow exit allows an active pool to accumulate. A wide exit keeps its level lower and clears it sooner after production stops.
scenes.caption: Changing an exit changes both amplitude and timing. A narrow exit allows an active pool to accumulate. A wide exit keeps its level lower and clears it sooner after production stops.
scenes.visual: Transform one generic blue pool between two cases. A narrow teal outlet produces a high level and long tail. A wide outlet produces a lower level and short tail. Label both 'schematic' and keep identical inflow arrows.
scenes.narration: Changing an exit changes both amplitude and timing. A narrow exit allows an active pool to accumulate. A wide exit keeps its level lower and clears it sooner after production stops.

scenes.tts: The same bookkeeping shapes time. Under constant input, an active pool rises toward a balance. When input stops, removal makes it decay. A faster removal process lowers the balance and clears the pool sooner.
scenes.caption: The same bookkeeping shapes time. Under constant input, an active pool rises toward a balance. When input stops, removal makes it decay. A faster removal process lowers the balance and clears the pool sooner.
scenes.visual: Draw two computed dimensionless curves from dX by dt equals input minus k times X. Use the same constant input for both and let both reach their own plateau before input switches off. Plot both curves on one shared absolute axis, active pool versus time, with no numbers. The faster-removal curve has a lower plateau; at the switch-off instant both start falling with the same slope, and the faster-removal curve falls below any small threshold sooner. Label 'computed model'.
scenes.narration: The same bookkeeping shapes time. Under constant input, an active pool rises toward a balance. When input stops, removal makes it decay. A faster removal process lowers the balance and clears the pool sooner.

scenes.tts: Some systems also build a slower adaptive brake while stimulation continues. A gap can let that brake reverse. Separated pulses offer recovery intervals that one steady input never provides.
scenes.caption: Some systems also build a slower adaptive brake while stimulation continues. A gap can let that brake reverse. Separated pulses offer recovery intervals that one steady input never provides.
scenes.visual: Show a yellow steady input bar above one pathway and separated yellow pulses above another. A teal brake gauge rises under the steady bar and partially falls in each pulse gap. Reveal the response gauges only after both patterns settle.
scenes.narration: Some systems also build a slower adaptive brake while stimulation continues. A gap can let that brake reverse. Separated pulses offer recovery intervals that one steady input never provides.

scenes.tts: Separated pulses can preserve responsiveness because each gap allows recovery. Constant input gives no such interval. Pituitary responses to gonadotropin releasing hormone show this contrast. In gonadotrope cells, the main adaptation appears to lie downstream of the receptor.
scenes.caption: Separated pulses can preserve responsiveness because each gap allows recovery. Constant input gives no such interval. Pituitary responses to gonadotropin-releasing hormone show this contrast. In gonadotrope cells, the main adaptation appears to lie downstream of the receptor.
scenes.visual: Reveal repeated response peaks beneath the separated pulses. Under the steady bar, the response shrinks as the teal brake grows. Add a careful label: 'GnRH: main block appears downstream'. Keep every trace labelled 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Separated pulses can preserve responsiveness because each gap allows recovery. Constant input gives no such interval. Pituitary responses to gonadotropin-releasing hormone show this contrast. In gonadotrope cells, the main adaptation appears to lie downstream of the receptor.

scenes.tts: Receptor uncoupling is therefore only one timer. G T P hydrolysis, messenger breakdown, and dephosphorylation set later timers. Each downstream layer fades when removal outruns production, and the slowest surviving layer can outlast the receptor's activity.
scenes.caption: Receptor uncoupling is therefore only one timer. GTP hydrolysis, messenger breakdown, and dephosphorylation set later timers. Each downstream layer fades when removal outruns production, and the slowest surviving layer can outlast the receptor's activity.
scenes.visual: Reassemble the full carried pathway. Three teal timers sit beside G-alpha, the messenger pool, and the target. Their hands finish at different moments. The receptor remains blocked at the top while the last downstream glow finally fades.
scenes.narration: Receptor uncoupling is therefore only one timer. GTP hydrolysis, messenger breakdown, and dephosphorylation set later timers. Each downstream layer fades when removal outruns production, and the slowest surviving layer can outlast the receptor's activity.

scenes.visual: End card shows one centered line only: 'Each downstream layer fades when removal outruns production.' No subtitle, logo, or smaller line.
